Abstract—Previous research indicates that many adults (nearly 40%)
fail to report their own documented child sexual abuse (CSA) when
asked about their childhood experiences. These controversial results
could reflect lack of consciously accessible recollection, thus bolstering claims that traumatic memories may be repressed. In the present
study. 175 individuals with documented CSA histories were interviewed regarding their childhood trauma. Unlike in previous studies.
